label: UI
blurb: A layout described as data, drawn by trusted components — no iframe, no script.

intents.doc: appended when a button is pressed; nothing executes

grid.doc: children in equal columns, one column under 700px

card.doc: a bordered panel; `accent` adds a left rule

tabs.doc: switchable panels; which one is open is per-viewer and never stored

heading.doc: a small uppercase label above a group

notice.doc: a called-out line; `label` is the bold lead-in

quote.doc: a quotation; `by` renders as the attribution

spacer.doc: vertical space; `size` is any CSS length

list.doc: a bulleted list of plain values

checklist.doc: tickable items; each item's `bind` is where its boolean lives, so a tick is readable back. An item with no `bind` renders disabled.

kv.doc: a definition list of label/value pairs. Both sides resolve a `{bind}`.

table.doc: a read-only table. `rows` are arrays, or objects keyed by column id. For a table the human edits, use the `table` TAB type.

stat.doc: one large number with a caption under it

image.doc: an image from assets/ or uploads/ only

link.doc: an anchor; `href` must be #, / or http(s)

button.doc: records an intent into state.intents and nothing else — it never acts

field.doc: an input that writes into state.data at `bind`. `field` is text, longtext, number, select or checkbox; `options` supplies a select.

gestures: whatever the agent described — buttons record an intent, fields write into the data model
a tabs component remembers which panel you had open, per viewer
notes: Catalog (25): col, row, grid, card, tabs, divider, spacer, title, heading, text, caption, badge, notice, quote, code, link, list, checklist, kv, table, stat, meter, image, button, field.
Where a prop takes both `value` and `text`, `value` wins.
`tone` takes a token NAME from `tones` above, never a hex. An unrecognised one draws the default, so `-apply` warns about it.
`image.src` must be under assets/ or uploads/; `link.href` must be #, / or http(s).
Any prop may be `{"bind":"path.in.data"}` instead of a literal — EXCEPT `field.bind` and `checklist[].bind`, which are the paths themselves.
An unknown component type renders a visible marker. An unknown PROP renders nothing at all, which is why `-apply` warns about one.
PREFER THIS OVER `html` whenever it can express the shape.
